summary.headline: Kaynes Q2 FY27 revenue INR 9,525 million with 13.2% EBITDA margin; smart meter revenue cut ~80% as receivables are prioritised.
summary.overview: Consolidated Q2 FY27 revenue was INR 9,525 million, EBITDA INR 1,256 million (13.2% margin) and PAT INR 398 million; H1 revenue INR 18,987 million with 14.1% EBITDA margin. Management deliberately moderated smart meter revenue to cut receivables, which fell from INR 1,402 million to INR 1,091 million quarter on quarter, while core EMS grew about 34% YoY. A restatement of FY26 and prior periods was made after a change to a new auditor, lifting FY26 PAT to INR 392 crore from INR 364 crore, and bill discounting was reclassified into borrowings, which raised reported debt. Management said Semicone Unit 2 and Circuits are now operational, with PCB revenue expected from Q3 FY27, and announced an initial agreement with Vishay for a 49% stake in the Semicone business, pending a definitive agreement.

financial_highlights.change: Smart meter revenue down ~80% YoY in Q2; core EMS up ~34% YoY to INR 799 crore
Down from INR 1,402 million in Q1 FY27; management target below INR 750 crore
Up from 163 days in previous quarter

segments.name: Core EMS (ex-smart meter)
segments.commentary: Q2 revenue about INR 799 crore vs about INR 595 crore a year ago (+34%). Management says EMS EBITDA was about 10.5% last year versus about 22% for smart meters.

segments.name: Smart meter
segments.commentary: Q2 revenue about INR 54 crore vs INR 228 crore a year earlier, about 80% decline; FY26 smart meter revenue about INR 960 crore. Management targets a deal with a partner for the business and expects smart meter at under 10% of revenue in H1.

segments.name: Aerospace and railway
segments.commentary: Management says these two segments grew more than 50% (aerospace more than 70%) and are the focus for higher margins. One railway product has received approval for commercial production.

segments.name: Semicone (OSAT) and Circuits (PCB)
segments.commentary: Semicone Unit 2 and Circuits are now operational, with several products in customer approval. PCB Unit 1 expected to generate revenue from Q3 FY27; both units targeted for full operation by Q4.

segments.name: Exports (August Electronics, North America)
segments.commentary: Export share is about 10% currently; target is 25%+ by 2030 under Mission 30. Growth has been slower due to global conflicts.

guidance_outlook: Management is confident of doubling revenue in FY27 and expects electronics business growth of more than 30% for the year.
H2 FY27 is expected to be stronger in both revenue and margins; profitability expected to normalise over the next quarters.

Management expects supply chain normalisation in the next two quarters, lowering lead times and input costs and allowing release of about INR 200-250 crore of strategic inventory, with review by end-December.
Vishay (Wishay) to take 75-90% of Semicone capacity; definitive agreement expected in 2-3 months, to be updated next quarter.
Smart meter receivable reduction plan (partner deal) to be presented at the next quarter's investor call; management says it is on track.
Management said there is no need to raise equity in the next 6 to 12 months, but framed this as a confident view rather than a formal commitment.
capex_capacity: Capex rose by INR 221 crore QoQ (net of subsidy): INR 115 crore in Semicone, INR 140 crore in Circuits and INR 21 crore in EMS, before a government subsidy recovery in Semicone of INR 59 crore.
Semicone Unit 2 and Circuits are operational; PCB Unit 1 to start revenue in Q3 FY27.
Application engineering for new semiconductor products takes 12-14 months from validation to commercial production; Vishay partnership is intended to shorten this.
Smart meter installation is slowed by government clearances; the company is holding meter supply until clearances are obtained.
demand_pricing: PCB is in global shortage, with lead times of 6-8 months and suppliers asking for advance payment; an engagement with a large EV maker (possibly North American) is progressing.
Commodity prices are elevated; wholesale inflation near 10% and manufactured products inflation at 8.4% in the quarter, raising costs across the supply chain.
The rupee moved from about 85 per USD in June 2025 to about 95 in the quarter; crude oil volatile, moving back about USD 100 in September.
Management says it is number 1 in smart meter installation and number 2 or 3 in supply to the government; CPSU/PCGL data cited, with a competitor's installations about 40% lower.

qa_highlights.question: What changed in the accounting for bill discounting that moved receivables into borrowings?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said bill discounting was earlier shown as a separate line item; it is now included in borrowings, which is why reported loans rose.

qa_highlights.question: Will the Vishay (Wishay) partnership take dedicated capacity or incremental capacity?
qa_highlights.answer: Vishay takes 75-90% of the Semicone capacity from existing lines; the rest is kept for existing customers, with management expecting Vishay to take the customer share to about 70%.

qa_highlights.question: How is the Vishay JV structured and will the 49% stake sit at Semicone level?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the 49% stake will sit at Semicone level for now; the definitive agreement is pending and may include an SPV or other structure, with Vishay's IP in a firewalled line.

qa_highlights.question: Quantify smart meter revenue and receivables for FY27 and the margin profile of the remaining business.
qa_highlights.answer: H1 FY27 smart meter revenue was about INR 270-290 crore; receivables fell from about INR 1,252 crore at the start of FY27. Management said smart meter share is below 10% of revenue and H1 EBITDA margin was 14.1%; at a 75:25 mix, margin would have been about 17.5-18%.

qa_highlights.question: Will the company need to raise funds in the next 6-12 months?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it is very confident it will not go to the market for equity; cash will come from the Vishay investment, smart meter collections and inventory release.

qa_highlights.question: Is the Vishay investment used for ISM 1.0 or ISM 2.0 commitments, and what is the smart meter partnership model?
qa_highlights.answer: Vishay investment is a loan from the parent that will return to the parent company. For smart meters, the company will keep manufacturing and give installation and O&M to a third party under a right-to-buy arrangement, retaining 51% control of the partnership.

risks_watch: Receivables: smart meter receivables still at INR 1,091 million; plan to cut below INR 750 crore and partner deal to be announced next quarter.

Debt and working capital: reported borrowings rose after reclassification of bill discounting; working capital at 169 days and inventory of INR 200-250 crore to be released only if supply chain normalises by end-December.
Margins: input cost inflation and the mix shift away from smart meters; management expects normalisation but has not quantified timing.
Semicone and Circuits product validation: customer approvals still pending; PCB revenue timing is Q3 FY27 and full operation Q4.
Restatement and auditor change: FY26 EBITDA margin restated to 14.2% from 15.8%; prior results were restated with a new auditor.
Vishay definitive agreement: 49% stake structure and timing still open; expected in 2-3 months.
Export share target of 25%+ by 2030 from about 10% today; North America growth slower due to global conflicts.
summary.management_tone: Confident on strategy and long-term growth, but cautious and somewhat defensive on the restatement, margins and smart meter receivables. Several answers on the Vishay structure were deferred to the definitive agreement, and the Q&A was disorganised, with some numbers restated or unclear in the transcript.
key_quotes: This quarter we choose to put balance sheet strength and cash discipline ahead of short-term revenue while continuing to invest ahead of time in the capabilities that will define Keynes over the next decade.
I am pleased to report that both are now operational and multiple products are receiving customer approvals.
Most importantly, as our strategic partner, Wishai will take up about 75 to 90% of the capacity which gives us a direct access to the global market other than China.
we are very very confident that we are not going to go to the market for the money

growth.why: Management targets doubling revenue in FY27 (electronics growth >30%), backed by operational Semicone Unit 2 and PCB Unit 1 (revenue from Q3 FY27), a ~INR 106,252m order book and Vishay taking 75-90% of OSAT capacity, though the definitive agreement is pending and PCB revenue may slip a couple of quarters; smart meter revenue is down ~80% YoY in Q2.

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.why: H1 EBITDA margin 14.1% with smart meter under 10% of revenue; management says H2 margins stronger and a 75:25 mix implies ~17.5-18%, though input cost inflation (WPI ~10%) and supply-chain normalisation timing are unquantified.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.why: Semicone Unit 2 and Circuits are already operational with PCB Unit 1 revenue due Q3 FY27 and full operation by Q4; INR 221 crore QoQ capex (net of subsidy) went in.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: Management targets doubling revenue in FY27 with EMS growth above 30% (core EMS +34% YoY to INR 799 crore in Q2) and an order book of about INR 106,252 million; smart meter volumes fell ~80% YoY, so growth depends on core EMS.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: Capex of INR 221 crore QoQ is already committed, but no new capacity plan is stated; the Vishay deal takes 75-90% of Semicone capacity from existing lines, so a fresh capex needs a definitive agreement first.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: Management is holding the FY27 doubling target and reports Q2 revenue of INR 9,525 million with H1 at INR 18,987 million, which would need a strong H2 to reach; no raise is signalled.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: Smart meter receivables still INR 1,091 million against a sub-INR 750 crore target, working capital rose to 169 days, and the INR 200-250 crore inventory release depends on supply normalisation by end-December.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: PCB Unit 1 revenue from Q3 FY27 and several Semicone products in customer approval, with one railway product approved for commercial production.

rows.label: Vishay 49% stake in Semicone
rows.why: Initial agreement announced with Vishay taking 75-90% of Semicone capacity, but the definitive agreement is pending and the structure (SPV or otherwise) is still open.

rows.label: Strategic inventory release INR 200-250 crore
rows.why: Release depends on supply-chain normalisation within two quarters; working capital already rose to 169 days from 163.

rows.label: Export share to 25%+ by 2030
rows.why: Exports are about 10% of revenue today and North America growth has been slower due to global conflicts.
